# A win32 program in C runs its tests in the C test agent, cross-compiled
# with MinGW's compiler and run under Wine in a prefix of the cache's, whose
# windows the null driver draws; the agent connects back to the driver over
# TCP, since Wine hands a Windows program none of the host's pipes
# (codegen/platform/win32/launcher.go). A build rooted at the component a
# test takes renders it as the package body would, and a test's trigger is
# the platform's #[gen.fires] for the event the program's handler is
# connected to: a button's press, a check box's state, an edit's text as it
# is typed and as Enter commits it. A node a branch renders is held while it
# is rendered and null once taken away, and a test taking no component
# builds the program's window.
#
# A snapshot is the window PrintWindow draws into a DIB section, sent to the
# driver as its pixels, which the driver encodes as a PNG. The component a test takes is shown
# in a window of its own, which grows as what it holds does: "Big" shows
# under the check box once the count passes one.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
exists app.sngl.snapshots/one.png
exists app.sngl.snapshots/big.png
! cmp app.sngl.snapshots/one.png app.sngl.snapshots/big.png

# The same agent built for 32-bit Windows, which draws what the 64-bit one
# did.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c --opt arch=386 app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'

# async.do runs its work on the loop, after the turn that posted it: C
# answers it with sngl_post, which the runtime defines as a message posted
# to the window every control is parked in, and a test's t.wait runs the
# loop while it waits.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c async.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# A handler the program wrote empty connects nothing, and a test can still
# trigger the event: it presses the button, which runs nothing.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c empty.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# The same programs in Go, which calls the runtime through the wrappers
# `sngl tool cgogen` writes (lib/platform/win32/cgo) and serves its tests
# over TCP as C's agent does, draw what C's drew: each snapshot is held to
# the one the C run wrote.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go --opt arch=386 app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go async.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go empty.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# A C struct of api's no wrapper crosses is still the wrapper package's, so
# the program's own literal of one builds in Go as in C.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c rect.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go rect.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# A function taking a ref is wrapped as every call of one is lowered, copy
# in and copy out: the wrapper takes the value and hands back the record of
# the result and each out, field for field the one the program declares,
# which converts it. It had no wrapper, and was called directly.

sngl generate --platform=win32 --lang=go -o out ref.sngl
grep 'GetClientRect__result\(cgo\.GetClientRect\(' out/main.go
! grep 'C\.GetClientRect' out/main.go
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go refrun.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# Calling C itself (the Go language's `cgo` option set to "direct"), Go
# compiles api's C beside the program and calls the function as C does. The
# whole program is called so: its snapshots are C's.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go --opt cgo=direct refrun.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go --opt cgo=direct app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
! sngl generate --platform=win32 --lang=go --opt cgo=cgo -o out app.sngl
stderr 'cgo="cgo": Go calls C "wrapper", "direct" or "purego"'

# A write to an element of a list C holds keeps the value before it takes
# the element's address: working the value out grows the list, which moves
# its elements, and the write lands in the list as it is after.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c store.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# A closure C calls back writes a local through its address, and what it
# writes is a copy that lasts the turn: the callback's call gives back the
# arena it used as it returns.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c callback.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# A closure C keeps and calls after the function that made it returned
# writes that function's local in a box: NoRef boxes a local a lifted
# lambda is handed the address of, as it boxes a var. It boxed only vars,
# so the local stayed a string the closure's state read as a box, and the
# program did not compile.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c retained.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

output {
    c {
        win32
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    var n = 0
    var name = ""
    var typed = ""
    var on = false
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text(value="Count {n}")
        ui.button #inc(text="More", @click { n += 1 })
        ui.button #dec(text="Less", @click { n -= 1 })
        ui.input #who(value=name, @input(v) { typed = v }, @change(v) { name = v })
        ui.checkbox #flag(checked=on, @change(v) { on = v })
        if n > 1 {
            ui.text #big(value="Big")
        }
    }
}

ui.window(title="Counter") {
    main()
}

func testPressesReachTheirHandlers(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.inc.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
    t.assert(c.big == null)
    c.inc.click()
    t.assert(c.big != null)
    c.dec.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
    t.assert(c.big == null)
}

func testValuesReachTheirHandlers(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.who.input("an")
    t.assert(c.typed == "an")
    t.assert(c.name == "")
    c.who.change("ann")
    t.assert(c.name == "ann")
    c.flag.change(true)
    t.assert(c.on)
    c.flag.change(false)
    t.assert(!c.on)
}

func testDrawsTheWindow(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.snapshot("one")
    c.inc.click()
    c.inc.click()
    t.snapshot("big")
}

func testTheWindowBuilds(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(true)
}
-- async.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component main ui.node {
    var log = ""
    var got = 0
    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #go(text="go", @click {
            var n = 6 * 7
            async.do(func() {
                got = n
            })
            log = "posted"
        })
        ui.text #shown(value=log)
    }
}

func testWorkRunsOnTheLoop(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.go.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.got == 42, 2000)
    t.assert(c.got == 42)
    t.assert(c.log == "posted")
}

ui.window {
    main()
}
-- empty.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component main ui.node {
    var n = 0
    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #b(text="b", @click {})
        ui.text("{n}")
    }
}

ui.window {
    main()
}

func testAnEmptyHandlerIsTriggered(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.b.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 0)
}

-- rect.sngl --
import api "sngl:platform/win32/api"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func width(right int) int {
    var r = api.RECT{left = 2, top = 0, right = right, bottom = 0}
    return r.right - r.left
}

component main ui.node {
    var right = 7
    ui.text("{width(right)}")
}

ui.window(title="x") {
    main()
}

func testARectOfTheProgramsOwn(t test.Test, c main) {
    t.assert(width(c.right) == 5)
}

-- ref.sngl --
import api "sngl:platform/win32/api"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func width() int {
    var r = api.RECT{}
    api.GetClientRect(api.GetFocus(), r)
    return r.right
}

ui.window(title="x") {
    ui.text("{width()}")
}

-- refrun.sngl --
import api "sngl:platform/win32/api"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func width() int {
    var r = api.RECT{right=-1}
    var ok = api.GetClientRect(api.GetFocus(), r)
    if ok == 0 {
        return -2
    }
    return r.right
}

component shown ui.node {
    ui.text("{width()}")
}

func testARefCallFillsItsStruct(t test.Test, c shown) {
    t.assert(width() >= 0)
}

ui.window(title="x") {
    shown()
}
-- store.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var held list[string] = ["a"]

func grow() string {
    held.push("b")
    held.push("c")
    held.push("d")
    held.push("e")
    return "z"
}

ui.window {
    ui.text("{held.length()}")
}

func testAWriteLandsAfterTheGrowth(t test.Test) {
    held[0] = grow()
    t.assert(held[0] == "z")
}

-- callback.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import macro "sngl:macro"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="calls.h", sources=["calls.c", "calls.h"])

#[c.native("sngl_int")]
func withInt(#[c.type("int_cb")] #[macro.retains] f func(i int), #[c.context] data c.pointer)

ui.window {
    ui.text("t")
}

func testAWriteFromACallbackOutlivesIt(t test.Test) {
    var got = ""
    withInt(func(i int) {
        got = "n{i}"
    })
    t.assert(got == "n5")
}
-- retained.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import macro "sngl:macro"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="calls.h", sources=["calls.c", "calls.h"])

#[c.native("sngl_keep_int")]
func keepInt(#[c.type("int_cb")] #[macro.retains] f func(i int), #[c.context] data c.pointer)

#[c.native("sngl_fire")]
func fire()

var out = ""

func arm() {
    var got = ""
    keepInt(func(i int) {
        got = "{got}n{i}"
        out = got
    })
}

ui.window {
    ui.button(text="arm", @click { arm() })
}

func testAKeptClosureWritesTheLocalItOutlived(t test.Test) {
    arm()
    fire()
    fire()
    t.assert(out == "n5n5")
}
-- calls.h --
typedef void (*int_cb)(int, void *);
void sngl_int(int_cb f, void *data);
void sngl_keep_int(int_cb f, void *data);
void sngl_fire(void);
-- calls.c --
#include "calls.h"
void sngl_int(int_cb f, void *data) { f(5, data); }
static int_cb kept;
static void *kept_data;
void sngl_keep_int(int_cb f, void *data) { kept = f; kept_data = data; }
void sngl_fire(void) { if (kept) kept(5, kept_data); }
